sources.title:
24K views · 439 reactions | On September 24, 2025, NASA successfully launched the Interstellar Mapping and Acceleration Probe (IMAP), along with two secondary spacecraft, aboard a SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket. The mission's primary objective is to map the boundaries of the heliosphere, the giant protective bubble created by the solar wind that shields our solar system from harmful cosmic radiation.

Launch and deployment details

Launch vehicle: A SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket launched from Launch Complex 39A at NASA's Kennedy Space Center in Florida.

Liftoff: The mission lifted off on Wednesday, September 24, 2025, at 7:30 a.m. EDT.

Rideshare payloads: In addition to IMAP, the rocket also carried NOAA's Space Weather Follow On-Lagrange 1 (SWFO-L1) and NASA's Carruthers Geocorona Observatory.

Orbital destination: All three spacecraft are traveling to the Sun-Earth L1 Lagrange Point, a gravitationally stable position approximately 1 million miles from Earth. They are expected to arrive in January 2026.

Signal acquisition: IMAP successfully established communications with mission control shortly after its deployment from the rocket's second stage.

Booster landing: The Falcon 9 first-stage booster successfully landed on the droneship "Just Read the Instructions" in the Atlantic Ocean.

Dennis Hlavsa /@dhlavsa with Space FrontPage and Launch Window Photo 

#NASA #SpaceX #falcon9 #IMAP #launchvideo #NOAA | Space FrontPage

excerpts.text: The two NASA Escape and Plasma Acceleration and Dynamics Explorers (ESCAPADE) Mars cubesats were supposed to launch as a rideshare on NASA’s Psyche mission. But the Psyche spacecraft wasn’t ready for its original launch window and had to wait a year. The [delay](https://spacepolicyonline.com/news/psyche-on-its-way-to-metal-rich-asteroid/) meant the trajectory to its destination, the asteroid Psyche, had to change and it no longer was headed in the right direction for ESCAPADE to reach Mars. Blue Origin offered to launch ESCAPADE on the first New Glenn launch, but the date kept changing and NASA [decided to forego](https://spacepolicyonline.com/news/its-a-scrub-for-the-inaugural-flight-of-blue-origins-new-glenn/) the offer at that time. They didn’t want to proceed with fueling the spacecraft, dubbed Blue and Gold, only to have to defuel them if there were more delays since it would add cost.

excerpts.text: NASA’s IMAP (Interstellar Mapping and Acceleration Probe) spacecraft arrived May 10, 2025, for processing at the Astrotech Space Operations Facility near the agency’s Kennedy Space Center in Florida. The mission will study how the Sun shapes the boundaries of the heliosphere, the bubble around our solar system. A semitrailer transported the spacecraft from NASA’s Marshall Space Flight Center in Huntsville, Alabama, after completing thermal vacuum testing, which simulates the harsh conditions of space, at the X-ray and Cryogenic Facility. Astrotech provides the facility and technicians to prepare the spacecraft for launch, including fueling and encapsulation. The IMAP spacecraft launched Sept. 24, 2025, on a SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket from Launch Complex 39A at NASA Kennedy. ||
